events.text: Houthi attacks on merchant ships in the Red Sea begin; ships start to avoid Bab el Mandeb and route round the Cape of Good Hope.
events.quote: After Yemen-based Houthi militia attacks on commercial ships transiting the Red Sea started in November 2023, some vessels began opting to avoid the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint

events.text: War risk premiums for the Red Sea mostly between 0.4 and 0.7 percent of hull value through 2024.
events.quote: Most of the time, it remained between 0.4% and 0.7%

events.text: War in the Middle East begins; 91 ships transit the Strait of Hormuz on 28 February and four on 8 March.
events.quote: falling to just four ships on March 8 from 91 seen on Feb. 28, according to S&P Global Commodities at Sea

events.text: Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz; Middle East to Asia VLCC rates reach their highest since at least November 2005.
events.quote: In March 2026, tanker rates for Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) leaving the Middle East to Asia were the highest since at least November 2005, when data were first recorded. The price increase followed Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz on March 2.

events.text: The Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman and the Persian Gulf are designated a Warlike Operations Area for seafarers.
events.quote: agree to designate the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman and Persian Gulf as a Warlike Operations Area (WOA)

events.text: The Baltic Exchange starts TD34, Gulf of Oman to China, as an emergency alternative to TD3C.
events.quote: Baltic Exchange has started an alternative to the TD3C route, which is on public trial currently. This emergency route is titled TD34 and is basis 270,000mt Gulf of Oman to China.

events.text: Iran shuts the strait again on the first day of a two week ceasefire.
events.quote: Iran has once again shut the Strait of Hormuz in response to Israeli strikes on Lebanon, casting serious doubt on the already fragile two-week Middle East ceasefire.

events.text: Iran and the United States sign a preliminary peace agreement to restore flows through Hormuz after 30 days of demining.
events.quote: On June 18, Iran and the US signed a preliminary peace agreement aiming to restore cargo flows via Hormuz

events.text: The ceasefire collapses after attacks on three merchant ships; transits fall to five in a night.
events.quote: Overnight into July 8, U.S. Central Command struck more than 80 targets inside Iran in direct response to Iranian attacks on three commercial vessels transiting the Strait.

events.text: Yemen based militants declare a maritime embargo on Saudi shipping; the Bab el Mandeb war risk premium rises from 0.3 to 0.5 percent.
events.quote: Reuters reported the premium level at 0.3% before the Yemen-based militants declared a maritime embargo on Saudi shipping July 20.

events.text: TD3C reaches WS1,318.75, a Baltic round trip TCE of USD 1,412,594 a day.
events.quote: climbed 115 points to WS1,318.75, which gives a daily round-trip TCE of $1,412,594

events.text: Hormuz traffic steady at 17 ships a day, with six VLCC transits on 25 October.
events.quote: The Strait of Hormuz had six VLCC transits on Oct. 25, the most since Oct. 17

events.text: Maersk expects all its services back through the Suez Canal by March 2027.
events.quote: A.P. Moller-Maersk expects all its shipping services to return to the Suez Canal by March 2027, according to a statement from the Suez Canal Authority (SCA).

canals.note: The study builds no tariff engine. Each canal toll is a lump sum input; a default exists only where a dated public source states a toll for a ship like the study's. None does for the Baltic standard ships: the Suez Canal Authority charges on Suez Canal net tonnage, which is not published for them, and the Panama Canal Authority's tariff could not be reached from this environment.

suez.why_empty: Suez tolls are levied on the Suez Canal net tonnage of the individual ship, in SDR per tonne by tonnage band, plus surcharges and less rebates. No public source states the SCNT of the Baltic's standard ships or a toll for them, so the toll is an input. The detour analysis reports the largest toll at which Suez still beats the Cape instead.

facts.text: Surcharge on crude oil tankers raised to 37 percent of normal transit dues laden and 27 percent in ballast, from 25 and 15 percent, for transits from 15 July 2026
quote: is amended to be 37% of the Suez Canal normal transit dues rather than 25%.
is amended to be 27% of the Suez Canal normal transit dues rather than 15%.
This periodical is applicable to tankers transiting the Suez Canal from the 15th of July 2026.

facts.text: The same 37 and 27 percent surcharges on petroleum products tankers
facts.quote: The surcharge levied on Laden "Petroleum Products Tankers" [Rate (2L) of the Transit Dues Schedule] transiting the Suez Canal in both directions, is amended to be 37% of the Suez Canal normal transit dues rather than 25%.

facts.text: Surcharge on dry bulk carriers raised to 22 percent of normal transit dues, laden or ballast, from 10 percent
facts.quote: The surcharge levied on (Laden/Ballast) "Dry Bulk Vessels" [Rate (3) of the Transit Dues Schedule] transiting the Suez Canal in both directions, is amended to be 22% from Suez Canal normal transit dues rather than 10%.

facts.text: A ship carrying one million barrels of crude (a Suezmax) pays roughly USD 500,000 to transit, according to the Suez Canal Authority
facts.quote: Ships carrying 1 million barrels of crude currently pay roughly $500,000 in tolls to transit the Suez Canal, while the latest LNG carriers pay between $300,000 and $500,000, according to the Suez Canal Authority.
facts.use: a scale reference for the break-even toll, not a default for the study's ships

facts.text: Southbound convoy transit 11 hours; waiting at most three hours
facts.quote: Shortening the transit time from 18 hours to 11 hours for the southbound convoy Minimize the waiting time for vessels to become three hours at most
facts.use: the canal day the study adds to a Suez routing (one day, against the 2 canal days the Baltic's TC20 TCE basis allows)

panama.why_empty: The Panama Canal Authority's tariff and calculator (pancanal.com) refuse this environment's connections. The only dated public toll found is the EIA's 2023 base toll for a product tanker in the Panamax locks, which is neither 2026 nor a bulk carrier, so P7's toll is an input and the TCE through Panama is reported before it.

facts.text: Base toll about USD 300,000 for a VLGC in the Neopanamax locks and USD 60,000 for a product tanker in the Panamax locks
facts.quote: the base toll to transit the canal is about $300,000 for a VLGC to cross the newer, larger Neopanamax locks. A smaller gas carrier, petroleum product tanker, or chemical tanker transiting the older, smaller Panamax locks has a base toll of $60,000.

facts.text: Unbooked first come, first served waits of 18 to 30 days were common in April 2026, according to a Panama based agent
facts.quote: unbooked First Come First Serve waiting times have lengthened materially and 18 - 30 days is common in many cases
facts.use: the waiting days scenario for an unbooked Panama transit

sections.name: Method
summary: How a detour is priced, and the dated events.

method: A detour is priced with the same engine at the same week's bunkers: the extra days and tonne miles against the base routing, and the freight at which the detour earns the base routing's TCE. For a premium the extra freight is the premium over the cargo net of commission; for waiting it is also the TCE the waiting days forgo, so it depends on the market's level.

War risk premiums are a percentage of hull value per transit period of seven days, from dated insurer and broker reports; hull values are Xclusiv Shipbrokers' five year old values of 7 September 2026. The Suez and Panama tolls, the ship to ship transfer's cost, the shuttle through the strait and the crew's war bonus have no public figure for these ships and are left out, and each panel says which.
